prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Meridian Regional Air Traffic Flow Management and Airport Collaborative Decision-Making System:Regional Flow Platform=Cedarbell;Meridian International Airport/Harbor East Airport/North Valley Airport/Lakeside Regional Airport/Southport Airport retain authority. Aliases:Airline Operations Coordinator=Saffron;Regional Flow Manager=Copperfin;Demand Prediction Service=Marlinstone;Weather Ingest Gateway=Orchard;Airport CDM Portal=Foxglove;Tower Supervisor=Brindle;Ramp Control Lead=Quartzline;Slot Allocation Engine=Blueharbor;Slot Coordinator=Halcyon;Tower Sequence Manager=Ironleaf;Ramp Movement Board=Skylark;Alert Distribution Hub=Lantern;Departure Metering Service=Emberline;Arrival Regulation Console=Nightjar(help-only). Airline Operations Centre→Airline Interface Adapter→Flight Data Exchange:Flight Intent Message;Identity Access Service authenticates;invalid/incomplete rejected(reason-codes);material intents supersede schedules;changes require messages. Cedarbell normalizes Airport Capacity Plan;Capacity Assessment Module updates Airport Acceptance Rate/runway/taxiway/sector/apron constraints. Blueharbor→Adapter/Foxglove:Calculated Takeoff Time/Target Off Block Time/arrival-opportunities;freeze:Pushback Window Token. Capacity>preferences;safety/emergency/humanitarian/national-obligation>commercial>discretionary;Ground Delay Program equity;changes justified;stands cannot override airspace. Orchard validates weather/provenance/overrides;Storm Cell Snapshot confidence/degradation/provisional-capacity visible;Meteorology Briefing Officer verifies. East Apron Sensor/West Apron Sensor→Skylark→Surface Surveillance Adapter→Foxglove:movements/milestones≤5s;validated occupancy/equipment-status→Skylark/Ironleaf. Quartzline→Blueharbor:Stand Tow Request Form;Brindle/Airport Duty Manager resolve conflicts;Runway Inspection Note precedes endorsement;North Runway Meter/South Runway Meter receive capacities. Modes:Normal Operations/Adverse Weather Mode/Capacity Reduction State/Recovery Phase(coordinated,commercial-logic-protected)/Contingency Fallback State(diversion/prioritization/communication/recovery). Saffron confirms plans/deferrals/revised-intents;Brindle distinguishes holds;Handling Resource Planner grades severity/suppresses recovery-duplicates;Ground Handling Dispatcher→Towbar;Aircraft Operator Representative supplies crew-legality. Substitution:Halcyon reviews Blueharbor exceptions/regional-objective

New part:
S688: The System Support Engineer investigates technical failures in submission, validation, or publication without altering the operational decision unless authorized through the defined control process.
S689: The Post Operations Report includes swap volume, rejection reasons, approval latency, compliance with revised times, and any equity concerns identified during the operating period.
S690: Aerodrome infrastructure events are treated as capacity inputs when they affect runway availability, taxi route usability, stand access, lighting performance, or supporting navigation services.
S691: The Regional Flow Platform records each event as an operational constraint with an effective time, expected duration, affected resource, confidence level, and approving authority.
S692: The Airport Duty Manager is responsible for ensuring that declared service reductions are entered promptly and that the operational description is consistent with local aerodrome control procedures.
S693: The Tower Supervisor uses the Runway Lighting Outage Card to confirm which runway lighting elements are unavailable before approving the operational status shown in the Tower Sequence Manager.
S694: When lighting performance limits night or low-visibility operations, the Capacity Assessment Module converts the limit into a runway configuration constraint rather than treating it as a general advisory.
S695: The Airport CDM Portal presents infrastructure events to authorized airport, airline, and flow management users as part of the shared operating picture.
S696: The Regional Flow Manager reviews the published constraint when it changes the usable runway rate, taxi-out predictability, or the feasibility of the active demand plan.
S697: The Capacity Assessment Module calculates the operational effect by comparing the affected resource with the current Airport Capacity Plan and the active weather state.
S698: If the event reduces arrival throughput, the Arrival Regulation Console applies the revised Airport Acceptance Rate after confirmation by the Regional Flow Manager.
S699: If the event reduces departure throughput, the Departure Metering Service updates metering rates and provides revised inputs to the Slot Allocation Engine.
S700: The Slot Allocation Engine uses the reduced capacity value to protect fairness while avoiding schedules that exceed the declared infrastructure capability.
S701: The Demand Prediction Service recalculates short-term demand against the constrained capacity so that delay and queue forecasts reflect the published limitation.
S702: The Tower Sequence Manager displays the accepted constraint to support runway sequencing decisions and to reduce conflicting tactical instructions.
S703: The Ramp Movement Board receives the same operational status so that apron movements can be coordinated with restricted taxi routes or stand access limitations.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
